title: Security Claims Matrix (Customer Questionnaires + RFPs) — Approved Language + Evidence Map
content:
PURPOSE
This sheet is the single source of truth for (a) approved security/compliance claims for questionnaires/RFPs and (b) what evidence exists + how to request it. If a customer asks something not covered here, do not improvise—route through the Exceptions Policy.

HOW TO USE
1) Find the closest prompt in the matrix (Ctrl+F by keyword).
2) Copy/paste the “Approved response” verbatim.
3) If “Evidence availability” is “Available (NDA)” or “Restricted,” follow the SOC 2 / Evidence Request Playbook.
4) If confidence is Yellow or Red, read “Notes / caveats” carefully and escalate if the customer wording is strict.

CONFIDENCE LEGEND
Green = Approved claim, generally safe as-written for Hosted/Dedicated/Private.
Yellow = True with deployment-mode nuance, contractual nuance, or limited configuration; use caveats.
Red = Not supported / not accurate / would be a roadmap commitment; use alternate language and/or Exceptions Policy.

IMPORTANT GUARDRAILS (DO NOT EDIT WITHOUT GRC/LEGAL)
- Do not state or imply: “ISO 27001 certified” (unless/ until we have a certificate).
- Do not promise “zero retention” unless explicitly scoped to a specific deployment configuration and confirmed by Security/GRC.
- Do not claim “customer data never leaves region” without reading the residency caveats (support access, control plane metadata, etc.).
- “We do not train foundation models on customer data” must be used as defined below (with definitions).

MATRIX (Tab: Claims)
Columns:
ID | Domain | Common questionnaire prompt | Deployment applicability | Approved response (copy/paste) | Evidence availability | Evidence / link pointer | Owner | Confidence | Notes / caveats | Last reviewed

SC-001 | Security program | Do you have a documented information security program with executive oversight? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Yes. Redwood Inference maintains a formal information security program with executive oversight, risk management, and documented policies and standards. The program is reviewed at least annually and updated as our product and risk profile evolves. | Available (NDA) | Program overview + selected policies via Evidence Request Playbook | Olga Petrov | Green | Provide high-level summary only in-line; share policies under NDA via GRC. | 2026-02-18

SC-002 | Compliance (SOC 2) | Are you SOC 2 compliant? Can you share your SOC 2 report? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood Inference undergoes an independent SOC 2 Type II audit. We can provide our SOC 2 report under NDA via our compliance evidence request process. | Available (NDA) | SOC 2 Type II report (restricted) | Daniel Carter | Green | Do not paste report content into questionnaires. Use “available under NDA.” | 2026-02-18

SC-003 | Compliance (ISO) | Are you ISO 27001 certified? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood Inference is not currently ISO 27001 certified. We maintain an information security program aligned with widely adopted security frameworks, and many of our controls map to ISO 27001/27002 themes. We can discuss control alignment and provide relevant evidence under NDA where appropriate. | Available (NDA) | ISO alignment one-pager (customer-facing) + evidence on request | Olga Petrov | Yellow | Use exact wording; do not say “certified” or “in the process of certification” unless approved. | 2026-02-14

SC-004 | Data protection | Do you encrypt data in transit? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Yes. Redwood uses industry-standard encryption in transit (TLS) for customer access to the API/Console and for service-to-service communications where applicable. | Public / Available | Security FAQ section “Encryption in transit” | Marcus Lin | Green | If asked about specific cipher suites, route to Security Eng. | 2026-02-19

SC-005 | Data protection | Do you encrypt data at rest? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Yes. Redwood encrypts data at rest for production systems that store customer data and service metadata, using industry-standard encryption mechanisms. | Available (NDA) | Architecture + encryption overview (deployment-specific) | Kevin Osei | Green | For Private/on-prem, clarify shared responsibility (customer-managed storage controls). | 2026-02-19

SC-006 | Key management | Do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) / KMS? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood supports KMS-based key management options by deployment mode. For Private deployments, customers can integrate with their own key management systems based on the agreed architecture. For Hosted/Dedicated, key management options depend on the selected deployment configuration and region. | Available (NDA) | Encryption + KMS one-pager (latest draft), architecture appendix | Naomi Feldman | Yellow | Do not promise “HSM” or “BYOK” universally; confirm per deal and deployment. | 2026-02-20

SC-007 | Access controls | Do you support SSO (SAML 2.0)? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Yes. Redwood Console supports SSO via SAML 2.0 for supported identity providers. | Public / Available | SSO/SAML/SCIM + RBAC capabilities page | Markus Klein | Green | If customer requires IdP-specific features, confirm supported IdPs list. | 2026-02-17

SC-008 | Access controls | Do you support SCIM provisioning? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood supports SCIM provisioning for user lifecycle management in supported configurations. | Available | SSO/SAML/SCIM + RBAC capabilities page | Markus Klein | Yellow | Some tenants/deployment types may require enablement; avoid “all plans by default” claims. | 2026-02-17

SC-009 | Authorization | Describe your RBAC model (roles/permissions). | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood provides role-based access control (RBAC) for the Console and API access management. Roles and permissions can be assigned to users/groups, supporting separation of duties for administrative and operational functions. | Available | RBAC capabilities summary (internal) + customer overview | Kevin Osei | Green | If customer needs a full permission list, share approved RBAC summary doc; do not screenshot internal admin. | 2026-02-17

SC-010 | Audit logging | Do you provide audit logs for admin/user actions? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Yes. Redwood provides audit logs for key administrative and access-related events in the Console and relevant API surfaces. Audit logs include timestamps and actor/context information and can be exported in supported configurations. | Public / Available | Audit logging customer overview | Marcus Lin | Green | Avoid claiming every single event is logged; use “key events” unless the customer provides a required list to validate. | 2026-02-19

SC-011 | Audit logging | Can audit logs be exported to our SIEM (Splunk, Sentinel, etc.)? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood supports audit log export options in supported configurations, including delivery to customer-managed destinations (e.g., object storage / SIEM pipelines). We can confirm the best integration pattern based on your SIEM and deployment mode. | Available | Audit logging export docs + examples (ENG-13988 / docs PR-2849) | Hanae Suzuki | Yellow | Confirm per destination; provide “supported patterns” not “native integration for all SIEMs.” | 2026-02-20

SC-012 | Retention/deletion | What is your default retention for prompts/outputs? Can we disable retention? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood’s data retention depends on deployment mode and configuration. We provide documented retention and deletion behavior for customer content and operational logs, and we can support enterprise retention requirements via deployment configuration and contractual controls where applicable. | Public / Available | Data retention + deletion overview | Olga Petrov | Yellow | Do not claim “we never store prompts/outputs” without confirming the specific product settings and contract. | 2026-02-19

SC-013 | Data use | Do you train models on customer data? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | No. Redwood does not train foundation models on customer-provided prompts, inputs, or outputs. “Train” here means using customer content to improve or retrain general-purpose models. Redwood may process customer content solely to provide the service (e.g., to generate outputs) and to maintain security and reliability (e.g., abuse prevention, troubleshooting) consistent with customer agreements and documented retention controls. | Public / Available | Security FAQ “Data use and training” section | Daniel Carter | Green | Do not shorten this to “we never use your data for anything.” Keep the definition of “train.” | 2026-02-18

SC-014 | Data residency | Can you guarantee all data stays in the EU? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood offers region selection and deployment options (including Private/VPC) to support data residency requirements. Data residency commitments are deployment- and contract-specific. We can describe the data flows for your chosen deployment and confirm what data is processed/stored in-region versus what may be accessed cross-region for support/operations under controlled processes. | Available | Data residency one-pager + data flow diagram (DES-2924) | Fatima Noor | Yellow | Avoid “guarantee” language without Legal + GRC signoff on the exact scope. | 2026-02-20

SC-015 | Privacy/GDPR | Do you support DPA and GDPR requirements? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood supports execution of a Data Processing Addendum (DPA) for applicable customers and maintains privacy and security controls designed to support GDPR obligations, including access controls, logging, and incident response. | Available | DPA template via Legal; evidence on request | Michael Grant | Yellow | Legal owns DPA language. Do not commit to specific clauses in-line. | 2026-02-15

SC-016 | Incident response | Do you have an incident response plan and breach notification process? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Yes. Redwood maintains an incident response program with documented processes for triage, containment, eradication, recovery, and post-incident review. Customer notification terms are addressed in customer agreements and applicable addenda. | Available (NDA) | IR policy excerpt + SOC 2 coverage | Marcus Lin | Green | Contractual breach notification timelines must come from Legal/contract. | 2026-02-18

SC-017 | BCP/DR | Do you have business continuity and disaster recovery plans? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Yes. Redwood maintains business continuity and disaster recovery planning appropriate to the service. Controls are evaluated as part of our security assurance activities, and we can share details under NDA where appropriate. | Available (NDA) | SOC 2 + BCP/DR overview under NDA | Daniel Carter | Green | Avoid quoting RTO/RPO unless a deal-specific SOW includes them. | 2026-02-18

SC-018 | Vulnerability mgmt | Do you perform vulnerability scanning and patching? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Yes. Redwood operates a vulnerability management program that includes regular scanning, prioritization, and remediation based on risk. | Available (NDA) | VM policy overview + SOC 2 | Kevin Osei | Green | If asked for exact frequency, use approved “regular/ongoing” wording unless Security confirms frequency. | 2026-02-16

SC-019 | Pen testing | Do you conduct third-party penetration tests? How often? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood conducts independent third-party penetration testing as part of our security assurance program. We can share a summary of results under NDA, subject to restrictions. | Available (NDA) | Pen test attestation/summary (restricted) | Marcus Lin | Yellow | Do not state a specific cadence (e.g., “annual”) unless confirmed for the current period. | 2026-02-16

SC-020 | SDLC | Do you have secure SDLC practices (code review, CI/CD controls)? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Yes. Redwood uses secure software development practices including peer review, CI/CD controls, and security testing appropriate to the service. | Available (NDA) | SDLC policy summary + SOC 2 | Naomi Feldman | Green | Avoid tool/vendor specifics unless requested; share under NDA if needed. | 2026-02-14

SC-021 | Subprocessors | Do you have a list of subprocessors / third parties? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Yes. Redwood maintains an up-to-date list of subprocessors and provides it through our standard customer-facing process. | Available | Subprocessor list via Legal/Privacy process | Michael Grant | Green | Provide canonical link/attachment only; do not paste stale lists into RFP docs. | 2026-02-15

SC-022 | Data isolation | Is customer data logically separated? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood implements tenant isolation controls appropriate to each deployment mode. Dedicated deployments provide isolated capacity, and Private deployments can be configured within a customer-controlled network boundary. | Available (NDA) | Architecture + shared responsibility summary | Colin O'Donnell | Yellow | Isolation mechanisms differ by mode; avoid “air-gapped” unless it is an on-prem/air-gapped package in scope. | 2026-02-19

SC-023 | Private/VPC | Can Redwood run in our VPC / on-prem? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood offers a Private deployment option, including VPC-based deployments and on-prem options for regulated or restricted environments, subject to scoping and support terms. | Available | Private deployment overview + scoping checklist | Colin O'Donnell | Green | Ensure customer understands control plane + shared responsibility boundaries; do not imply “customer manages everything” by default. | 2026-02-19

SC-024 | HIPAA/BAA | Will you sign a BAA / are you HIPAA compliant? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood can discuss HIPAA requirements for healthcare use cases, but HIPAA suitability and BAA execution are subject to product scope and Legal review. Please engage Redwood Legal early for any BAA requests. | Available | Exceptions Policy + Legal intake | Michael Grant | Red | Do not say “HIPAA compliant” as a blanket claim. Escalate immediately. | 2026-02-13

SC-025 | Logging/content | Do you log customer prompts/outputs for debugging? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood’s handling of customer content is documented and depends on deployment mode and configuration. Where operational logging involves customer content, Redwood limits access and retention and applies access controls and auditing. | Available | Retention/deletion overview + access control section | Olga Petrov | Yellow | Customers often interpret “logging” broadly; ask what they mean and respond with the documented retention policy. | 2026-02-19

SC-026 | Customer access | Can customers access audit logs via API? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood provides audit log access and export options in supported configurations. API availability and export patterns depend on deployment mode; Redwood can confirm the best approach for your environment. | Available | Audit logging overview + export docs | Hanae Suzuki | Yellow | Do not claim “full API coverage” if the customer requires specific endpoints; validate requirements. | 2026-02-20

SC-027 | Monitoring | Do you have security monitoring and alerting? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Yes. Redwood operates security monitoring and alerting for the service, including detection and response processes aligned to our incident response program. | Available (NDA) | SOC 2 + monitoring overview | Marcus Lin | Green | Provide high-level only; details under NDA. | 2026-02-18

SC-028 | Data deletion | Can you delete our data upon request? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood supports customer data deletion consistent with the deployment mode, configuration, and contractual requirements. Redwood provides documented deletion behavior and timelines for customer content and relevant service data. | Public / Available | Data retention + deletion overview | Daniel Carter | Yellow | Don’t promise custom deletion SLAs in questionnaires; route to contract/SOW if required. | 2026-02-19

SC-029 | Access to production | Who can access production and customer data? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Access to production systems is restricted to authorized personnel based on role, least privilege, and business need, and is logged and reviewed. Access to customer content is controlled and limited consistent with documented processes and customer agreements. | Available (NDA) | Access control policy excerpt + SOC 2 | Kevin Osei | Green | If customer requests named personnel lists, decline and escalate via GRC. | 2026-02-18

SC-030 | Roadmap trap | Do you support (feature X) in audit logs / retention / SSO? | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Redwood can confirm current capabilities for your deployment and provide documentation for what is supported today. We avoid committing to future features in security questionnaires; any future capabilities must be evaluated separately and, if agreed, captured in a written statement of work. | N/A | Exceptions Policy | Olga Petrov | Green | Use this when a questionnaire tries to force roadmap commitments. | 2026-02-12

TAB: EVIDENCE INVENTORY (summary)
- SOC 2 Type II report: Restricted, NDA required, request via GRC (Daniel Carter)
- Pen test summary: Restricted, NDA required, request via GRC (Marcus Lin)
- Policy excerpts (IR/BCP/Access control/VM/SDLC): Restricted, NDA required, request via GRC (Olga Petrov)
- Customer-facing one-pagers: Shareable, latest versions linked from Enterprise Security Enablement Kit index

OPEN ITEMS / FOLLOW UPS
- Confirm final customer-facing wording for “audit log export destinations” once docs PR-2849 is merged (Owner: Hanae; Due: 2026-03-01)
- Align “Hosted retention defaults” language with PM-4860 (Owner: Naomi/Olga; Due: 2026-03-05)
- Add Private deployment ‘shared responsibility’ paragraph to reduce misinterpretation in RFPs (Owner: Colin; Due: 2026-03-08)

CHANGE CONTROL
Edits to the “Approved response” column require review by GRC + Security (and Legal where contractual language appears). Log edits in the enablement-kit links/version tracker and reference the updated FAQ version in outbound RFPs.
